articles.title: Gold price slides to one-year low, heads for worst year since 2015
articles.summary: Gold fell to a one-year low on Monday as elevated Treasury yields, a stronger dollar and expectations of tighter monetary policy weighed on demand, putting bullion on course for its worst annual performance in more than a decade, Reuters reported.According to a Reuters analysis, prices dropped to $3,830.74 a troy ounce, their lowest level since October 2, 2025. Gold has fallen 31.5% since reaching a record $5,594.82 in January and is heading for its worst year since 2015.“Markets expect higher interest rates ahead, boosting the dollar and compounding gold’s headwinds, leaving it exposed to deeper declines,” Nikos Tzabouras, senior financial editorial writer at FXCM, told Reuters.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe dollar is trading near its highest level since April 2025, making dollar-denominated bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies and weakening demand in recent months.Treasury yields have also risen as markets price in a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate increase in December, along with a smaller probability of a 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Volatility in Nvidia shares has added to the pressure. The chipmaker’s market value fell by $1.9 trillion from early October to $3.9 trillion as of Friday, potentially prompting investors to sell gold to raise cash.“In the short term gold is a liquidity asset … the thing you sell to raise cash,” Nicky Shiels at MKS PAMP told Reuters.Middle East war fuels inflation concernsThe US-Israeli war against Iran, which began in late February, has driven oil prices higher, adding to inflation and fueling expectations of tighter monetary policy worldwide.Although non-yielding gold is traditionally viewed as a hedge against inflation, it tends to lose appeal when interest rates rise because it does not generate income.Physically backed gold exchange-traded funds attracted 211 metric tons of inflows during the third quarter despite higher bond yields and a stronger dollar. Demand for bars and coins, however, declined sharply.Also Read: Morgan Stanley turns bullish on global stocks, targets S&P 500 at 8,700Central-bank demand may weakenCentral banks remained active buyers earlier in the year, purchasing an estimated 675 tons between January and September, according to the World Gold Council.Demand from this segment could slow after Poland, the year’s most active official buyer, reached its target of 700 tons of gold reserves in November. Its central-bank governor nevertheless left open the possibility of additional purchases.China remained a rare source of strength. Its central bank has purchased gold for two years, supporting domestic investment sentiment.Despite the selloff, gold has so far remained above the psychologically important level of $3,800 an ounce.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: Dow sinks 700 pts, Nasdaq over 2% as Huang exit fuels tech rout ahead of Nvidia Q3 earnings
articles.summary: US stocks fell sharply on Monday as Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO deepened the selloff in AI shares, putting greater focus on the chipmaker’s Tuesday earnings and Anthropic’s IPO later this week.The S&P 500 lost 143.26 points, or 1.89%, to end at 7,418.41 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 620.16 points, or 2.47%, to 24,516.11. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 721.40 points, or 1.38%, to 51,626.15.Losses accelerated through the session, pushing the S&P 500 and Dow down more than 1% each. The Nasdaq tumbled over 2%, weighed down by a 4.6% drop in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.For live updates on US Markets, click here“It’s the back-and-forth in this market of the AI-related stocks catching a bid versus this rotation trade,” Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird in Louisville told Reuters. “Over the last couple of weeks, it’s like a day-to-day thing where, you know, some days the AI names absolutely rip and then the very next day, you know, they’re in a freefall.”“There are signs underneath the surface that investors aren’t panic-selling and running away from the asset class altogether, but are probing other corners of the equity market,” Mayfield added.Nvidia fell 4.2%, leading every member of the Magnificent Seven group of megacap technology stocks lower. Huang’s resignation following allegations of an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China added to existing concerns about AI’s rapid expansion and potential risks.Huang’s abrupt departure also prompted the Trump administration to announce new restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia. The move came ahead of US President Donald Trump’s expected meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.The selloff marks a sharp reversal for semiconductor stocks. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had gained 106.6% for the year by mid-June, but its advance has since narrowed to about 43%. That is still roughly four times the S&P 500’s gain in 2026.Also Read | Michael Burry warns of 'mild manipulation' in Nvidia's China sales. What Big Short investor expects for the stockThe retreat has pushed the Nasdaq more than 10% below its record closing high from October 6, confirming that the index is in a correction.Nvidia is expected to report a 90.4% year-over-year increase in earnings on revenue of $109.10 billion.Warsh comments and rate outlookFederal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said Monday that technological advances could significantly affect the economy. Potential outcomes range from stronger growth with broadly shared gains to higher unemployment and an economic slowdown if expected investment returns fail to materialise.Investors are awaiting minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee’s latest meeting, due Wednesday, for clues about the policy path ahead of next month’s interest-rate decision.Markets see a 96% probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase in December, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Among individual stocks, chipmakers Intel and Micron declined sharply, alongside AI cloud providers CoreWeave and Nebius. Major cloud companies Alphabet, Amazon and Meta also ended substantially lower, while server makers Dell and Super Micro Computer posted steep losses.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: Indian equities ride global AI trade unwind: Is D-Street back on foreign investors' radar? BNP Paribas answers
articles.summary: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) have returned to Indian equities with purchases worth nearly $8 billion over 15 trading sessions, as global investors reassess their exposure to AI-linked stocks, offering a fresh boost to Dalal Street after nearly two years of sustained foreign selling. Between October 21 and November 10, foreign investors bought approximately $8 billion worth of Indian equities, reversing around 16% of the nearly $50 billion they had sold over the preceding two years, according to a report by BNP Paribas.The renewed foreign buying has coincided with a strong recovery in domestic equities, with the benchmark Nifty50 gaining around 10% over the past one month."The return of foreign capital comes against the backdrop of significant selling in other Asian markets. FIIs sold $9 billion worth of equities in South Korea and $26 billion in Taiwan, while major regional indices came under pressure. Over the 30-day period cited in the report, the Nasdaq declined around 7%, South Korea's KOSPI fell 16% and Japan's Nikkei dropped 10%.ALSO READ: Coal India's 3rd big windfall in a year? How Mahanadi Coalfields IPO could unlock Rs 8,964 croreBNP Paribas said India was capturing a portion of the global portfolio rotation away from the AI theme. The investment bank attributed the shift to concerns over whether returns on capital would justify the substantial expenditure on AI infrastructure and the possibility of a slowdown in AI spending."The recent decline in AI-linked equities appears driven by market concerns regarding the scale of returns on capital relative to significant capital expenditures and expectations of a slowdown in AI spending," the brokerage said.The shift in global flows has coincided with an improvement in India's domestic macroeconomic environment. Crude oil prices have declined, US 10-year Treasury yields have eased from 5.3% to around 5.1%, and multiple rating agencies have upgraded their GDP growth forecasts for India.The rupee's appreciation against the US dollar has also supported foreign investor returns. BNP Paribas noted that the USD/INR exchange rate moved from 95.8 to 94.3, further enhancing dollar-denominated returns for FIIs.The improvement in investor sentiment has also been reflected in market performance. The Nifty gained around 10.5% over the past month, significantly outperforming the midcap index, which rose 3.7%, and the smallcap index, which gained just 0.5%.IT, telecom lead initial foreign buyingThe initial return of foreign investors was concentrated in the information technology and telecommunications sectors.ALSO READ: Saw the rally coming? How India's mutual funds raised stakes in 11 Nifty stocks before rebound to gain bigAccording to BNP Paribas, NSDL data showed that FII buying in the second half of October was heavily concentrated in these two sectors. Foreign investor holdings in Indian IT stocks increased to $45 billion in October from $37 billion in September, while telecom holdings rose to $39 billion from $35 billion.However, the report noted that market performance in November indicated that the rally had started broadening beyond these sectors into the wider largecap universe.FII holdings in Indian equities stood at $685 billion in October, marginally lower than $689 billion in September, indicating that the recent return of buying had yet to translate into a meaningful month-on-month increase in overall holdings.Largecaps emerge as beneficiariesThe return of foreign investors has coincided with a shift in domestic investor preferences towards largecap stocks, providing an additional source of support to the segment.Flows into pure largecap mutual funds increased around 20% month-on-month to Rs 10 billion in October, while inflows into large and midcap funds surged 99% to Rs 85 billion. In contrast, growth in inflows into midcap and smallcap funds decelerated by 38% and 29%, respectively.BNP Paribas said, "We continue to prefer large caps," arguing that the segment was benefiting from the twin tailwinds of FII buying and retail investors shifting allocations away from small- and midcap-oriented schemes.The investment bank added that the convergence of foreign and domestic buying was providing a significant advantage to largecap valuations."We observe a twin tailwind for Indian large-cap stocks driven by shifting investor flows," the brokerage said, adding that the convergence of FII and retail buying was providing a significant advantage to largecap valuations.Valuations are also relatively more attractive in the largecap segment. The report puts largecap valuations at 18.4 times price-to-earnings, compared with 23.1 times for midcaps and 21.8 times for smallcaps.Largecap earnings growth of around 20% year-on-year in the second quarter of FY27 has also helped narrow the earnings growth gap with smaller companies.Domestic flows remain supportive, but liquidity is tighteningWhile foreign investors have returned, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) have continued to play an important role in supporting the market.DIIs bought $6.5 billion worth of equities in October, even as FIIs sold $2.2 billion during the month. However, domestic mutual fund flows moderated, with overall equity scheme inflows declining 14% month-on-month to Rs 330 billion in October. Systematic investment plan (SIP) inflows remained relatively stable, declining 1% to Rs 321 billion.At the same time, mutual fund cash holdings declined to $18.4 billion, or 3.8% of assets under management, the lowest level since July 2024.BNP Paribas described the shift in domestic investor allocations as a "flight to quality", adding that the rotation from SMID stocks towards largecaps, alongside increased inflows into liquid funds, suggested that investors were becoming more cautious.The brokerage noted that 95% of bond fund inflows were concentrated in liquid and money market funds, indicating a growing preference for cash management.The report also flagged elevated equity supply, with IPOs and qualified institutional placements remaining high for the third consecutive month.Despite the moderation in mutual fund flows, retail participation remained visible, with 3.4 million new demat accounts opened during the month, the highest monthly addition since January 2026.However, the ratio of discontinued or completed SIPs to new registrations increased to 1.17, with new SIP registrations falling to 5.1 million and discontinued SIPs rising to 5.9 million.BNP Paribas cautioned that a sustained reading above one in the SIP stoppage ratio could be negative for future SIP flows.The return of foreign investors, therefore, comes at a time when domestic flows remain substantial but signs of tightening liquidity are emerging within the mutual fund industry.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. articles.title: Belrise Industries shares jump 11% as Q2 profit rises 25% YoY; revenue grows 17%
articles.summary: Belrise Industries shares rallied 10.50% to Rs 237.78 during Monday’s trading session after the company reported 25% year-on-year (YoY) growth in profit after tax (PAT) and a 17% increase in revenue from operations for the September quarter (Q2 FY27).Belrise Industries Limited (BIL), an integrated automotive component manufacturer, announced its financial results for Q2 FY27 and the first half of FY27, reporting growth in both revenue and profitability.The company's revenue from operations increased 17% YoY to Rs 2,746 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2,353 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. Profit after tax (PAT) rose 25% to Rs 166 crore from Rs 133 crore in Q2 FY26.Belrise Industries Q2 FY27 business highlightsThe company's manufacturing revenue grew 26% YoY to Rs 23,441 million in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 18,601 million in the year-ago quarter. Manufacturing EBITDA increased 19% to Rs 3,170 million from Rs 2,663 million in Q2 FY26. Manufacturing EBITDA margin stood at 13.5% during the quarter. Additionally, 71% of the company's manufacturing revenue came from powertrain-neutral products.Belrise Industries H1 FY27 performanceFor the first half of FY27, manufacturing revenue increased 23% YoY to Rs 45,420 million, compared with Rs 36,923 million in H1 FY26. Manufacturing EBITDA rose 15% to Rs 5,963 million from Rs 5,199 million in the corresponding period last year. The manufacturing EBITDA margin stood at 13.1%, while powertrain-neutral products accounted for 71% of manufacturing revenue.Belrise Industries secures new ordersDuring the quarter, Belrise Industries secured several new orders across its commercial vehicle and two-wheeler and three-wheeler businesses. The company won a programme from a leading Indian commercial vehicle manufacturer to supply complete chassis frame assemblies across its heavy commercial vehicle (HCV) platforms. The supplies will be made from a new facility in Dharwad, with production expected to ramp up from Q1 FY28.The programme is expected to add Rs 60,000–1 lakh in content per vehicle, with peak annual revenue potential of Rs 1,500–2,000 million.Belrise also entered complete three-wheeler body manufacturing after being selected as the second source for complete body and chassis assemblies for a high-selling model of a leading Indian two-wheeler and three-wheeler manufacturer. The order represents incremental content of approximately Rs 9,000 per vehicle.Production from its new facility at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is expected to ramp up from Q1 FY28, with peak annual revenue potential of Rs 1,000–1,200 million.In its suspension business, the company onboarded its sixth original equipment manufacturer (OEM) customer, a leading premium two-wheeler manufacturer in South India. Supplies commenced in Q3 FY27. It also secured additional orders from a growing two-wheeler and three-wheeler OEM, with production expected to begin in Q4 FY27.What management saidCommenting on the company's Q2 and H1 FY27 performance, Shrikant Badve, Managing Director of Belrise Industries, said the quarter was marked by strong execution and a healthy demand environment. He highlighted that manufacturing revenue grew 26% YoY to Rs 23,441 million, while adjusted PAT increased 25% to Rs 1,663 million.Also read: Tata Motors PV shares crack 9% as Motilal Oswal cuts earnings estimates, stays bearish after Q2 resultsThe company also secured its maiden Letter of Intent (LoI) for the supply of CNC fixtures to an ecosystem partner of one of the largest American smartphone companies.According to Badve, India's electronics manufacturing ecosystem is poised to become one of the country's largest and most cost-competitive manufacturing segments. The new order will provide Belrise with an opportunity to demonstrate its precision engineering capabilities developed over the years.Share PriceBelrise Industries shares have rallied 45% over the past one year. The stock is currently trading at a market capitalisation of Rs 21,567 crore. Jimmy Tata accuses Noel of 'backdoor takeover'
articles.summary: Jimmy Naval Tata, younger brother of late Ratan Tata and one of the longest-serving trustees of Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), has accused Noel Tata of using the charitable institutions to consolidate family control over Tata Sons, calling the induction of multiple family members into the trusts a “back-door takeover” of the group’s holding company.In a detailed written response to a senior trustee on the state of affairs at Tata Trusts and controversies surrounding the group, Jimmy has also criticised changes to Tata Sons’ Articles of Association, backed chairman N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment and called on the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to enforce the listing of Tata Sons without delay.Also Read: Jimmy Tata breaks silence on Tata matters; backs Chandra staying chair & Tata Sons listing, opposing Noel's stance“What has transpired in recent time is that the trusts are being filled with family members of the present Tata Trust Chairman, thereby securing a degree of control over Tata Sons that was never the settlors’ intention,” he said, adding that having more than one family member on a trust was inappropriate.“Such an arrangement is untenable and amounts to a back-door takeover of Tata Sons,” he said.Jimmy’s intervention is significant as the 85-year-old trustee has largely stayed away from trust meetings and voting and has rarely publicly articulated his views on the ongoing differences within the group.He said the two principal Tata trusts were established by Sir Ratan Tata and Sir Dorabji Tata for public welfare and that trustees were custodians of their assets, not owners. He cited their founding objectives, including poverty alleviation and safeguarding Indian culture, and said the institutions should remain focused on serving the people of India.Jimmy traced the current governance differences to amendments made to Tata Sons’ Articles of Association around 2013-14, which he said had fundamentally altered the relationship between the charitable trusts and the operating company.He argued that the earlier framework kept the welfare trusts separate from Tata Sons’ commercial operations, while subsequent amendments gave the Tata Trusts chairman veto powers and the ability to place directors, undermining the collective authority of the board.He also questioned differences in trustee tenure rules, alleging that they had compromised independence and enabled the marginalisation of dissenting trustees.Also Read: Noel Tata warns Tata Sons listing could put profits ahead of philanthropy, says it may change the ‘Tata way’Citing Venu Srinivasan, whose term expires in December, he alleged that Srinivasan was being targeted for opposing the induction of Noel Tata’s son into SRTT. He also referred to the earlier removal of Vijay Singh.Jimmy contrasted the current situation with the past, when independent figures such as Nani Palkhivala, Gautam Sarabhai, Homi Sethna and Homi Bhabha served as trustees.On the differences over Chandrasekaran’s continuation as Tata Sons chairman, Jimmy praised his leadership, saying he had turned around companies burdened by severe debt and delivered record earnings and substantial dividend payouts.“Despite Chandrasekaran receiving overwhelming support (including 4–1 in Tata Sons board and a unanimous resolution passed by Tata Trusts), Noel sought to block him arbitrarily by invoking the onerous veto provisions in the amended Articles of Association without providing any justification or accountability,” he said.Jimmy’s comments come amid a widening rift between Noel, chairman of Tata Trusts, and the Tata Sons board over Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, the proposed listing of the holding company and the group’s governance structure.Tata Trusts collectively owns about 66% of Tata Sons, with SRTT holding 23.56%. Its position is central to decisions concerning the future of the holding company and the wider conglomerate.Jimmy said listing Tata Sons was critical to improving transparency and accountability and restoring the separation between the charitable trusts and the commercial operations of the group.“Listing would dismantle the pervasive culture of secrecy, impose statutory accountability, and necessitate rewriting the onerous Articles of Association to restore the pre-1989 separation between business operations and welfare trusts,” he said.He also warned against any attempt to restructure Tata Sons into smaller entities to avoid regulatory listing requirements, saying this would be contrary to public and shareholder interests.Jimmy called on the RBI to enforce strict timelines for listing and urged the government and the Charity Commissioner to intervene to protect the original objectives of the trusts.The RBI has classified Tata Sons as an upper-layer non-banking financial company (NBFC), requiring it to list its equity shares on a recognised stock exchange within three years of being identified in that category. The central bank has rejected Tata Sons’ application to surrender its core investment company registration, requiring it to comply with the regulatory framework applicable to upper-layer NBFCs.Also Read: Tata International appoints T V Narendran as Chairman and Noel N Tata as Chairman Emeritus effective November 12Jimmy has been a trustee of SRTT since 1989 and is one of its three perpetual trustees, the others being Noel Tata and Jehangir Jehangir. He is the younger son of Naval Tata and his first wife Sooni Commissariat. Noel Tata is Naval Tata’s son from his second marriage to Simone Dunoyer.Jimmy, who lives in Pune, has historically preferred correspondence to participation in trust meetings. During a 2016 interview, he showed reporters a file containing hundreds of letters through which he had communicated his views to trustees and board members.He is also the second-largest individual shareholder of Tata Sons after Noel Tata, with a 0.81% stake, or 3,262 shares, according to estimates based on investment banking data.

articles.title: FPI buying hits 5-year high in November. What's driving the $7.5 billion inflow?
articles.summary: Mumbai: In a sharp U-turn after months of sustained selling, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) pumped $7.5 billion into Indian equities in the first 10 trading sessions of November - the highest monthly inflow in five years, according to Bloomberg data.This comes after FPIs withdrew $2.17 billion from Indian equities in October and $3.46 billion in September. The net investments in November so far are the highest since November 2021. The last time foreign investors pumped in more money in a single month was November 2020, when inflows stood at $9.56 billion, the data showed.135868866According to fund managers, FPIs have been aggressively investing amid a correction in AI-related stocks globally and a decline in crude oil prices. "The FPI flows are driven by multiple factors. profit booking on AI Investments, drop in oil prices, election results in Brazil, correction in Indian valuations over last two years, talks of exemptions on capital gains and reduction in rupee volatility," said Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra AMC.All this came in quick succession and the combined effect is visible in FPI flows, he said.Read more: IPO calendar: Mahanadi Coalfields among 3 companies to raise over Rs 10,000 cr in busy week for primary marketBrent crude prices have fallen nearly 21% to $93.37 per barrel on November 13 from a peak of $118 on October 30. The Indian rupee has appreciated by ₹1.97, or about 2%, against the US dollar since the beginning of October, rising from ₹96.22 per dollar to ₹94.25 per dollar by mid-November.Domestic institutional investors, meanwhile, have turned net sellers, booking profits amid a sharp rally in the market, after providing a crucial backstop through much of the year. DIIs have sold equities worth over ₹49,000 crore in the first 10 trading sessions of November, according to NSE data. Since the beginning of November, the Sensex and Nifty have gained nearly 10% each, while the BSE MidCap 150 and BSE SmallCap 250 indices have advanced around 8% each.Read more: Will Sensex, Nifty continue their bull run or consolidate? 4 factors to watch out for this weekOverseas investors began 2026 with net outflows of $3.26 billion into Indian equities in January, before turning net buyers in February with investments of $1.69 billion. However, the respite was short-lived, as March saw a sharp reversal, with FPIs pulling out $13.23 billion - their biggest monthly sell-off.Their return to Indian equities reflects both global portfolio rotation away from AI-heavy markets and improving outlook for India, said Anurag Byas, director for global markets solutions at Rothschild & Co. "Lower crude prices, better earnings and now attractive valuations seem to have supported this sentiment change. This is a positive signal but may be early to be extrapolated; the fundamentals must improve and the oil and currency stability must hold for this to become a sustained trend," he said. Shah of Kotak Mahindra AMC expects FPI flows to move in line with how the above factors interplay with each other.

We do not consider a further rate hike in February advisable, given the proximity to the union budget," State Bank of India chief economic adviser Soumya Kanti Ghosh wrote in a report last week."The December 25-bps hike to be followed by a more data-dependent policy approach. This also leaves room for a downward revision in terminal-rate expectations," the report said.Indranil Pan, chief economist at Yes Bank said, "A hike in April remains a possibility, but the probability of the same may have weakened due to cooling global crude prices and steadying rupee."Brent prices fell sharply in early November as markets responded to expectations that the US would avoid another major military offensive after Democrats took control of both houses in the US.The recent correction in crude oil prices has tempered expectations of a relatively aggressive hiking cycle, with markets scaling back bets on multiple rate increases in the coming MPC meetings.Domestic inflationary risks also remain, due to the potential impact of El Nino, which could push up food prices.
